# Cinematic UI — Style Prompt

> Software filmed like a movie. The app's own interface floats as a dark slab in a true black void, tilted steeply away from a low, close camera so lines of text run diagonally and shrink into the distance. Only a razor-thin band is sharp: one menu item, one typed line, one figure; everything nearer and farther melts into bokeh. A soft pool of light lies on the slab and trails whatever matters. The camera never stops drifting and never moves fast. The UI acts on its own (a badge arrives, rows resolve, a reply types itself, a button presses) and the film hard-cuts on the action. The only wide shot is the payoff. It ends quietly: one line of white type on black, then a still logo.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

A product film for **apps, dashboards, digital services and any screen the user owns**: a shop's order app, a class platform, a booking page, a creator's link page. The protagonist is the real interface rebuilt in code, faithful to the product, and the cinema comes only from camera, focus and light.

Not a screencast (no cursor, no zoom-to-click, no keycaps, no callouts), not a stage talk (no typed headline on a stage, no piling UI, no number inserts on a grid), not a phone showcase (no device, no pastel void, no lift-out cards), not a sizzle reel (no beat grid, no flashes, no shake, no glows). No captions explain the UI: the UI shows itself.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Stage**: `--void`, true black, outside the UI. No wallpaper, haze, floor or gradient. Corners are already black from the light falloff; a lens vignette (`radial-gradient(120% 95% at 50% 50%, transparent 50%, 70 % black 100%)`) is added only in the wide shot and in flagged shots, where a screen-space layer is needed anyway.
- **The slab**: the app at its native size (1600 × 1000 px in the 16:9 example, a 900 × 1640 phone-width layout in 9:16), radius 14, a 1 px hairline at 9 % of `--teks` and a faint top highlight at 7 %. Panels step from `--latar` (window) to `--latar-2` (lists, cards). Real-looking density: twelve plausible orders, names, IDs, amounts, statuses.
- **Camera**: the slab is one plane under `perspective` (1200-1400 px for close shots, 2000-2600 px for the wide), transformed `translate3d(drift) rotateY(yaw) rotateX(pitch) rotateZ(roll) scale(mag)` about the focal point, so roll applies first, then tilt, then yaw.
- **Depth of field without animated blur**: two copies of the slab share the camera. Bottom: the sharp copy, where every UI change happens. Top: a copy blurred once (`filter: blur(b) brightness(0.72)`, b = 3.4-6 UI px, so it grows with magnification on screen) in its own layer, masked with an inverted band: transparent along the focal line, opaque away from it, feathered over about 1.8× the band's half-width. The mask is a `linear-gradient` at `180° − roll`, the plane's depth direction. Neither the filter nor the mask changes during a shot.
- **Crisp macros**: the sharp copy is laid out at `zoom: Z` (Z ≈ magnification, rounded, 1-4) and the plane scaled by `mag / Z`, so text is rasterised at the size it is filmed. The blurred copy is laid out at 1× and scaled by Z.
- **Light on the plane**: a layer above the copies, inside the same transform: a core ellipse (transparent to 45 %, 22 % black at the edge) offset 12 % toward the far side and toward the roll's side, over a spill ellipse with seven stops ending in black. Spill radius = share of frame width ÷ magnification, longer along the line of action. Because it is on the plane, the tilt foreshortens it into an egg that changes with every camera. It is painted once per shot and only moved and grown by transform. In the wide shot the light opens up completely, so the layer is dropped.
- **Flag**: in about a third of shots, a screen-space soft edge (75 % black, 20 % feather) cuts one side of the pool, at least 25° off the text diagonal.
- **Crop to the light**: everything past the spill is black, so each layer (sharp copy, blurred copy, light) is sized to the box the pool covers during the shot, including where it travels. The frame looks identical and the browser paints far less.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the app's window, `--latar-2` its panels and rows, `--teks` primary text (85-90 % white on the default), `--teks-redup` secondary text (45-60 %). A brand's background becomes the app's chrome: a pale brand gives a light app floating in the same black void.
- `--utama` is the product's own primary colour: the selected nav badge, the send button, today's bar. `--teks-di-utama` on it.
- `--aksen` only fills a reference chip (an order number in the composer), with `--teks-di-aksen`.
- Fixed, as the product's own status colours: green `--hijau` (paid), amber `--kuning` (unpaid), sky `--langit` (ready), each a filled pill with its own dark text token.
- Fixed for the look: `--void` (black stage, light and flag gradients mixed from it) and `--void-teks` (95 % white closing type and logo mark). No tinted light, no glow, no added accent: if a colour is not in the app, it is not in the film.

## 4. Type

- **`--font-isi`** carries the whole UI at native size: nav 26 px, rows 24 px, labels 19-22 px, buttons 600 at 24 px, status pills 600 at 19 px. In focus on screen it is 70-130 px tall; in the wide shot it stays at least 22 px.
- **`--font-judul`** carries the app's headings (600, 40 px, −0.02 em), the big figure in the total card (600, 64 px, tabular, −0.03 em), and the closing line: weight 500, 90 px at 1080 high (76 px + a 60 px tagline line in 9:16), −0.02 em, `--void-teks`.
- **Mono** (`--font-kode`, IBM Plex Mono 400): order IDs and chips.
- Defaults: Inter for both; any clean product sans suits (Space Grotesk, Poppins). Never a display or script face: the film's typography is the product's.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Camera drift is linear** over the whole shot and still moving at the cut: track 3-10 % of frame width (up to 22-35 % for a long pan along rows or with a caret), push 2-5 %, turn 1-1.5° of roll. No easing to a stop, no shake.
- **Shot lengths follow the action**: punctuation shots (a nav item, a button, a figure) 1.5-2.3 s, process shots (a list resolving, a reply typing, the payoff) 2.2-3.6 s. The action starts 0.15-0.4 s after the cut and its result holds 0.5 s before the next cut.
- **Rack focus**: over 0.45-0.7 s on a smoothstep ease-in-out, a second blurred layer masked at the new focus fades in while the first fades out, so the sharp band moves without repainting anything. The light pool follows the focus as a 0.35 s moving average, so it arrives just after.
- **Appear**: opacity 0 → 1 over 0.35 s on `power3.out`, rows staggered 0.1 s top to bottom; a single small item (a badge) also rises 12 px.
- **Select**: a pill fills over 0.35 s ease-in-out while the label goes from 60 % to full.
- **Typing**: 12.5 characters a second, caret solid while typing, blinking at 1.6 Hz when idle; the focus follows the caret.
- **Press**: scale 0.97 in 0.08 s, back in 0.2 s, a 22 % dark overlay as the pressed colour.
- **Payoff changes**: statuses cross-fade 0.3 s staggered 0.14 s, a total counts up over 1.4 s with an ease-out cubic, a bar grows from 40 % on `power3.out`.
- **Ending**: dim the last UI shot to black in 0.4 s, the line fades 35 % → 95 % white in 1.2 s, the tagline joins 0.9 s later over 0.6 s while the line re-centres; 0.3 s dissolve to the logo, which holds completely still.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | Expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Extreme macro, 4-6×, pitch 40-48°, roll ±15-24°, band one word deep | the detail that starts everything | a new badge; a tab; a "paid" stamp; a send button |
| Macro, 2.5-4×, pitch 38-44°, the camera tracking with a caret | something being done, by itself | a reply typed; a search; a price edited; a caption written |
| Medium, 2-2.5×, pitch 30-36°, long pan along rows, rack to one row | quantity, reading, the problem in a list | orders piling; unpaid invoices; students' submissions; comments |
| Wide, 0.95-1×, flat-on (pitch and roll 0), push 5% | the payoff: everything changing at once | all orders paid; a full schedule; a finished page |
| Hard cut back to a macro after the wide | the one result that matters | the total; the rating; the booked seat |
| Dim to black, one line, still logo | release and memory | name and tagline; contact |

The diagonal flips sign on every cut (roll − then +), so two macros in a row read as two camera positions. Cuts are hard between UI shots; only the ending dims and dissolves.

## 7. Native moves

- **The thin plane.** One word sharp on a steep diagonal, the rest of the app dissolving into bokeh above and below. *Fits content like:* "12 baru" on an orders menu; a course's "Modul 3" unlocking; a creator's subscriber count; the first line of a chapter in a reading app.
- **The UI acts alone.** No cursor anywhere: a pill fills, rows resolve top to bottom, a button presses with its own pressed colour. *Fits content like:* a booking slot taken; homework marked done; a playlist sorting itself; a ticket checked in.
- **The caret follow.** A reply types itself at 12.5 characters a second while the camera and the light travel with the caret, then the focus racks to the send button. *Fits content like:* a shop confirming a pickup time; a tutor answering a parent; a podcast host writing show notes; a story's last sentence.
- **The only wide shot.** After all the close-ups, the whole window near-frontal while several regions change at once; then straight back to a macro of the figure. *Fits content like:* every order turning paid and today's income climbing; a timetable filling; a dashboard of a fundraiser reaching its goal.
- **The quiet ending.** One line on black growing from grey to white, the tagline joining it, then a logo that does nothing. *Fits content like:* an app name and promise; a class title and its start date; a channel name and handle.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Flat frames.** If a shot looks like a screenshot, raise the pitch before anything else; in-focus text must run diagonally and near text be 1.4-1.8× far text.
- **Everything in focus** means the band is too wide or the shot too wide. Only the payoff is mostly sharp.
- **Blurry macros**: never scale a 1× layer by 5; lay the sharp copy out at `zoom` close to the magnification.
- **Animated blur** costs every frame. Keep the blur and the masks static within a shot; rack focus by cross-fading two masked layers, never by tweening `filter` or `mask-image`.
- **Live preview budget.** Only the sharp copy animates smoothly; the blurred copy changes in a few single steps (a typed line per word, a counter in two jumps, rows all at once). Animate UI content with opacity rather than transforms, change counters in coarse steps, cache element lookups, and `display: none` the UI shots that are not on screen. A plane tilted in 3D that fills the frame is slow to draw in a phone browser, so the wide shot is flat-on (the source allows 8-12° of pitch; keep it at 0 unless the preview can afford it). No grain layer: a full-frame overlay costs every frame on phones.
- **A centred round spotlight** reads as a hole in a black overlay. The pool lives on the plane, offset toward a key, longer along the action, trailing the subject.
- **Subjects drifting out.** The drift is linear, so plan where the focal point is at the end of the shot (caret end, rack target) and keep it inside the frame.
- **Adding colour**: no glows, rings, flares or tinted light. A brand colour shows only where the app itself uses it.
- **Explaining**: no captions, arrows or labels over the UI; if a beat needs words, they are in the UI itself.
- **Brand fonts** wider than Inter: give rows and the closing line room, or shorten the copy; don't shrink the in-focus text.

## Measured from the source

The source direction gives these numbers for a 1920 × 1080 film, which the example keeps: magnification 5-7× (extreme macro), 2.5-4× (macro), 1.5-2.5× (medium), 0.8-1.1× (wide); pitch 35-50°, 30-45°, 25-40°, 8-12°; roll ±12-20° flipping sign every cut; yaw ±5-15°; perspective 1100-1500 px (1800-2200 wide); sharp band 4-8 %, 8-15 %, 15-30 %, 50-70 % of frame height; maximum blur 24, 20, 14, 6 px; spill radius 0.32-0.38, 0.40-0.45, 0.48-0.55, 0.70-0.80 of frame width along the action; average luminance 4-10 %; typing 12-13 cps; appear 0.35 s; select 0.35 s; press 0.08 s + 0.2 s; rack 0.4-0.8 s; outro type 90 px weight 500, −0.02 em; logo mark about 115 px with a 0.4× gap, held still. The source film runs 45-55 s with 8-10 shots (process shots 5-9 s, punctuation 2-3.5 s); this recipe compresses it to 17 s with six beats, keeping the alternation of long and short shots, the single wide payoff and the still ending.

# Cinematic UI: beat plan

Default length 17 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.2, medium 3, long 3.6.

## hook

- en: extreme macro (5x) on one nav item or badge, tilted 42°, only it sharp; it highlights by itself while the camera drifts
- id: makro ekstrem (5x) pada satu menu atau lencana, miring 42°, hanya itu yang tajam; menyala sendiri sambil kamera melayang

## problem

- en: medium shot along a list resolving top to bottom, a long pan across the rows, focus racking to the row that hurts
- id: shot sedang menyusur daftar yang muncul dari atas ke bawah, kamera menyisir baris, fokus pindah ke baris yang bermasalah

## fact

- en: macro on one value or status in the app, the rest melting into bokeh; the pool of light trails onto it
- id: makro pada satu angka atau status di aplikasi, sisanya lebur jadi bokeh; kolam cahaya menyusul ke situ

## step

- en: macro on a field: text types itself at 12.5 characters a second, the camera drifts with the caret, a button presses
- id: makro pada kolom isian: teks mengetik sendiri 12,5 huruf per detik, kamera ikut kursor, lalu tombol tertekan

## compare

- en: two hard-cut macros of the same app, the diagonal flipped: before state, then after state of one row
- id: dua makro dipotong keras di aplikasi yang sama, diagonal dibalik: keadaan sebelum, lalu sesudah pada satu baris

## number

- en: the only wide shot: the whole window near-frontal, statuses flip and a total counts up; then a hard cut to the figure
- id: satu-satunya shot lebar: seluruh jendela hampir frontal, status berubah dan total naik; lalu potong keras ke angkanya

## proof

- en: extreme macro on a confirmation the app shows itself (a paid badge, a sent tick), held, still drifting
- id: makro ekstrem pada konfirmasi yang muncul sendiri di aplikasi (lencana lunas, centang terkirim), ditahan sambil melayang

## offer

- en: macro on the price or plan line inside the app's own UI, a thin focal band across it, no added badges
- id: makro pada baris harga atau paket di dalam UI aplikasi sendiri, pita fokus tipis melintas, tanpa tempelan tambahan

## cta

- en: dissolve to the still logo and name in white on black, one quiet contact line, nothing moves for 2 s or more
- id: larut ke logo dan nama diam, putih di hitam, satu baris kontak redup, tidak ada yang bergerak 2 detik atau lebih

## payoff

- en: dim to black, then one centred line fades from 35% to 95% white; the tagline joins it and the line re-centres
- id: meredup ke hitam, lalu satu baris di tengah naik dari 35% ke 95% putih; tagline menyusul dan baris kembali ke tengah

    <meta charset="UTF-8" />

    <title>UI sinematik</title>
    <script src="/_lib/gsap@3.15.1/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>

      @font-face { font-family: "Inter"; src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,"); font-weight: 600; }
      @font-face { font-family: "IBM Plex Mono"; src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,"); font-weight: 400; }
      /* Token brand (recipes/README.md): brand mengganti dua belas nilai pertama dan menjadi warna aplikasinya.
         Panggungnya tetap hitam pekat: kekosongan, bukan latar brand. */
      :root {
        --latar: #0c0d10; --latar-2: #17181d; --utama: #4c7dff; --aksen: #a495ff;
        --teks: #e3e4e8; --teks-redup: #8b8d95; --teks-di-utama: #ffffff; --teks-di-aksen: #15112b;
        --utama-di-latar: #7097ff; --aksen-di-latar: #b4a9ff;
        --font-judul: "Inter", "Noto Sans", sans-serif; --font-isi: "Inter", "Noto Sans", sans-serif;
        /* Milik tampilan ini: hampa hitam, teks penutup putih 95 %, status aplikasi (warna produk), mono. */
        --void: #000000; --void-teks: #f2f2f2;
        --hijau: #2fbf71; --hijau-teks: #03200e; --kuning: #f2b544; --kuning-teks: #2a1b00; --langit: #5ab0f0; --langit-teks: #04182a;
        --font-kode: "IBM Plex Mono", "Noto Sans", monospace;
        --garis: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 9%, transparent);
        --sorot: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 7%, transparent);
        --batang: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 16%, var(--latar-2));
      }
      * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }
      html, body { width: 1920px; height: 1080px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--void); }
      #root { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: var(--void); -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }
      .scene { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; visibility: hidden; background: var(--void); }
      #s1 { visibility: visible; }

      .rig { position: absolute; will-change: transform; }

      .redup { background: var(--void); opacity: 0; will-change: opacity; }
      /* Aplikasi rekaan (pencatat pesanan toko kue), warna dari token brand. */
